entities.summary: Jacob of Juterbogk was a German monk and theologian. Benedict Stolzenhagen, known in religion as Jacob, was born at Jüterbog in Brandenburg of poor peasant stock. He became a Cistercian at the Paradyż Abbey in Poland, and was sent by the abbot to the University of Kraków, where he became master in philosophy and doctor of theology. He returned to his monastery, of which he became abbot. In 1441, however, he was discontented with the absence of strict discipline in his community, he obtained the leave of the papal legate at the council of Basel to transfer himself to the Carthusians, entering the monastery of Salvatorberg near Erfurt, of which he became prior.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent theologian and philosopher, Jacob of Juterbogk's teachings influenced the development of Cistercian thought in Europe, shaping the intellectual landscape of the region during the 15th century. His transfer to the Carthusians also contributed to the growth of this monastic order.
